title: Perspective & Form
subtitle: Boxes, cylinders and balls in space

lessons.title: The Horizon Line
lessons.summary: Eye level and the vanishing point.

steps.title: Your eye level
steps.text: The horizon line is always at your eye level. Lines that go straight away from you, like train tracks, all meet at one spot on the horizon called the vanishing point. Things get smaller the further away they are.

steps.title: Above and below
steps.text: Look at a box below your eye level and you see its top. Lift it above your eye level and you see its bottom instead. Right on the horizon, you see neither.

steps.title: Train tracks
steps.text: Trace the horizon, both rails and the sleepers. Every rail line heads to the vanishing point.
steps.hint: Use quick, straight pulls. Rails first, then the sleepers across them.

quiz.question: Where do train tracks seem to meet?
choices: At the vanishing point on the horizon
At the bottom of the page
quiz.explain: Parallel lines going away from you meet at the vanishing point.

lessons.title: One-Point Box
lessons.summary: A box with its front facing you.

steps.title: Box in one-point
steps.text: In one-point perspective, the front of the box faces you as a flat square. Its sides go back toward one vanishing point. Draw the front square, run lines from its corners to the point, then close the back where you want the box to end.

steps.title: Your box
steps.text: Trace the box. The faint lines show where its edges head.
steps.hint: Front square first, then the edges that go back, then the back edges.

quiz.question: In one-point perspective, the box's front face is...
quiz.explain: Only the sides recede; the front stays square.

lessons.title: Two-Point Box
lessons.summary: A box with a corner pointing at you.

steps.title: Corner first
steps.text: Turn the box so a corner points at you, and its sides now head to two vanishing points, one on each side of the horizon. Vertical edges stay straight up and down.

steps.title: Two-point box
steps.text: Trace the box. Its top edges head toward the two dots on the horizon.
steps.hint: Start with the front vertical edge, then the top edges.

quiz.question: A two-point box shows you...
choices: A corner pointing at you, with sides going to two points
quiz.explain: Each side heads to its own vanishing point.

lessons.title: Cylinders
lessons.summary: Two ellipses joined by straight sides.

steps.title: Ellipses change with eye level
steps.text: A cylinder is two ellipses joined by straight sides. An ellipse near your eye level looks thin and flat. The further below your eyes it goes, the rounder it gets. Watch the can sink below the horizon.

steps.title: Draw a can
steps.text: Trace the can: a full ellipse on top, the front half of the bottom, and two straight sides.
steps.hint: The bottom curve is rounder than the top, because it's further below your eyes.

quiz.question: A cup far below your eye level: its top ellipse looks...
quiz.explain: The further from eye level, the more you see into it, so it gets rounder.

lessons.title: Spheres
lessons.summary: Wrap lines around a ball to show its turn.

steps.title: Balls with lines
steps.text: A ball's outline is a circle from every side. To show which way it's turned, draw lines that wrap around it, like the equator and lines from pole to pole. The way they curve shows the angle.

steps.title: Wrap a ball
steps.text: Trace the circle, then the two curved lines that wrap around it.
steps.hint: Draw the circle, then let each curve hug the ball.

quiz.question: From any side, the outline of a ball is...
quiz.explain: That's why the wrapped lines are needed to show which way it faces.
